name: Developer Portal (developers.fuzefront.com) — approval frames
description: Design-first UX contract for the standalone Fuze developer portal: home (signed-out + personalized signed-in), the aggregated OpenAPI catalog, the spec viewer with its embedded OpenAPI render, the sandboxed 'Try it' playground, and My access. States are contract here, not decoration — the catalog's nothing-harvested-yet and harvest-failed cases, the viewer's invalid-spec fail-closed case, and the playground's 429 quota-exceeded, sandbox-target-unavailable (with an explicit no-production-fallback statement) and 403 cases each have a frame. Approving a flow approves its slice of the build inventory, so implementation cannot invent a different component/package layout. frontend-test-engineer drives Playwright against these via the data-frame / data-* hooks.

designSystemAdditions: CodeBlock — read-only, copyable monospace surface with an optional header bar and language/tone spans, for request/response bodies, validator output and code samples. NOT in @fuzefront/design-system today; forms/CodeField is an editable input, not this. frontend-engineer adds it as a foundation PR before the spec-viewer and playground flows are implemented.

TreeNav — collapsible hierarchical navigation (product → service → spec, and tag → operation). navigation/ currently has only Breadcrumb and Pagination; shell/MenuItem is a flat item. Foundation PR, never one-offed.

Badge — HTTP method tone map (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE → the existing cyan/success/warning/error semantic tokens). The colors already exist; the method→tone mapping is the addition, so every Fuze surface that renders an HTTP method renders it identically.

Already in the base and reused as-is, NOT re-invented: ProgressMeter (composed into QuotaMeter), StatusCallout, EmptyState, Skeleton, Spinner, StatusPill, Badge, Button, IconButton, ExternalLink, SearchField, Select, Input, Textarea, CodeField (multiline → request body), DataTable, Tabs, Breadcrumb, TopBar, UserMenu, Avatar.

frames.label: 01 · Home (signed out)
frames.summary: Anonymous landing: hero, quick links with the Playground shown locked, the providesTo product directory, and the sandbox-safety promise stated before sign-in.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Renders with data-auth='anonymous'. Catalog is reachable read-only; Playground and My access quick links carry data-locked='true' and are shown DISABLED, never hidden — the developer must learn the capability exists and that it needs sign-in. data-action='sign-in' starts the Authentik OIDC redirect; data-action='browse-catalog' routes to /catalog without auth. The product directory renders one [data-product] card per .fuze/manifest.json providesTo entry that has at least one published spec. [data-safety-notice='sandbox-only'] is present on the signed-out page too — the no-production promise is not gated behind sign-in.

frames.label: 02 · Home (signed in, + empty first sign-in)
frames.summary: Personalized home: quota strip, 'your recent specs', 'your sandbox activity', and both panels' empty variant for a developer's very first sign-in.
frames.acceptanceNotes: data-auth='authenticated' and [data-membership-status='active'] render from GET /me/access. [data-panel='quota-summary'] shows used/limit from GET /sandbox/quota with data-quota-used and data-quota-limit; the meter fill tone escalates to warning >80% and danger at 100%. [data-panel='recent-specs'] and [data-panel='sandbox-activity'] come from GET /me/activity and show ONLY the signed-in developer's own data (DevPortalPlayground:view_history never returns another developer's calls). With zero history each renders its empty variant ([data-empty='no-recent-specs'], [data-empty='no-sandbox-activity']) which must onboard with a CTA, not merely state emptiness. Activity rows render the HTTP method via the method-tone Badge and the target's real status code, including non-2xx.

frames.label: 03 · Catalog (populated)
frames.summary: Product → service → spec TreeNav rail, search and product/tag/sandbox-mode filters, and result cards carrying version, operation count, harvest age and sandbox mode.
frames.acceptanceNotes: GET /catalog with q/product/tag/sandboxMode. [data-panel='catalog-tree'] renders collapsible nodes with data-tree-node='<product>' and '<product>/<service>' and data-expanded true/false; selecting a node filters the result list without a full page load. Every result card carries data-spec='<product>/<service>', data-spec-version, data-harvested-at and exactly one [data-sandbox-mode] of mock|sandbox|unavailable — a developer must be able to see, before opening a spec, whether Try-it will work. A spec whose last harvest failed validation still appears, badged data-sandbox-mode='unavailable', and links to the invalid-spec state rather than being hidden. [data-result-count] reflects the filtered count; [data-action='clear-filters'] resets every filter and the search box.

frames.label: 04 · Catalog states (loading / empty / error / 403)
frames.summary: Loading skeletons, cold-start empty (nothing harvested yet), filtered-empty, harvest-failed error degrading to a badged stale catalog, and the 403 not-a-Developer fail-closed case.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Five distinct states, each independently addressable by data-state. (a) loading: skeletons preserve the populated layout, results region aria-busy='true'; no spinner-only screen. (b) empty [data-empty='no-specs']: zero specs in the registry is a COLD START, not an error — copy links to the publish-spec CI guide rather than dead-ending. (c) empty-filtered [data-empty='no-results']: specs exist but the query matches none; states the total and offers data-action='clear-filters'. (d) error [data-error='harvest-failed']: the catalog serves the last known-good snapshot, and EVERY row plus a page-level chip carries [data-catalog='stale'] with the snapshot timestamp — cached data is never presented as fresh. With no cache at all the list is replaced by [data-empty='catalog-unavailable'] and no stale rows are shown. (e) forbidden [data-http='403']: Permit denied DevPortalCatalog:read; fails closed with no partial catalog, and routes to /access.

frames.label: 05 · Spec viewer (overview + OpenAPI render)
frames.summary: Three panes: operations grouped by tag, our aggregated overview plus the selected operation (parameters, request/response schemas, example), and copy-paste code samples.
frames.acceptanceNotes: GET /specs/{specId}. [data-panel='spec-header'] renders name, version, source repo, spec path, harvest age, OpenAPI version and operation count — provenance is always visible so a developer knows which commit's contract they are reading. [data-panel='endpoint-list'] groups operations by tag with method-tone badges and data-operation='<operationId>'. [data-panel='operation'] renders parameters and request schema ([data-panel='request-schema']) and every declared response ([data-panel='response-schema']) including 4xx/5xx — not just the 2xx. The OSS renderer embed (Stoplight Elements / Swagger UI per plan §3) is themed with fuse-seam tokens; the chrome around it is ours. data-action='try-it' and data-action='try-it-operation' carry the current operation into the Playground prefilled. Code samples substitute the SANDBOX base, never a production host.

frames.label: 06 · Spec viewer states (loading / fetch failed / invalid / 404 / stale)
frames.summary: Loading skeletons, 502 spec-fetch failure, the invalid-spec fail-closed case with validator output and Try-it disabled, 404 not found, and the stale-spec badge.
frames.acceptanceNotes: (a) loading: the header renders from catalog data already held, so only the panes awaiting the blob show skeletons and nothing reflows on arrival. (b) [data-error='spec-fetch-failed'] with data-http='502': the catalog entry exists but the document could not be retrieved; offers retry, back-to-catalog and a raw download, and explicitly states it is not an account problem. (c) [data-state='invalid-spec'] is the load-bearing case: a document that parses but is not valid OpenAPI must NOT render a partial doc page. The renderer is replaced by the validator output ([data-code='validation-errors']), the source repo is named for the report action, the last valid version is offered, and [data-action='try-it'][data-try-it='disabled'] is DISABLED-and-visible rather than hidden — a request builder generated from a half-parsed spec would produce calls for operations that do not exist. (d) [data-empty='spec-not-found'] with data-http='404' for a removed/renamed spec. (e) [data-state='stale']: renders normally but badges the age; we mark staleness rather than hiding it.

frames.label: 07 · Playground (request builder / response / quota)
frames.summary: The 'Try it' panel: sandbox target selector, request builder, response panel, quota meter, own-call history, and the permanent never-touches-production notice.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Three things are ALWAYS visible and non-dismissible: [data-safety-notice='sandbox-only'], the resolved target ([data-resolved-target] + [data-sandbox-mode]), and [data-panel='quota']. The authorization header row is NOT editable and is marked [data-security-note='synthetic-identity'] — a developer must be unable to paste a real production token into a sandbox call, and the proxy mints a synthetic identity scoped to the target. [data-input='request-body'] is prefilled from the spec example and validated against the operation schema before send. data-action='send-request' POSTs /sandbox/requests. [data-panel='response'] shows status ([data-response-status]), duration ([data-response-time]), size, body/headers/trace tabs and states that values are schema-generated, not from a real database. [data-panel='request-history'] shows only the signed-in developer's calls.

frames.label: 08 · Playground fail-closed states (429 / target down / 403 / 5xx)
frames.summary: Sending, locally-blocked invalid request, 429 quota exceeded, sandbox target unavailable with an explicit no-production-fallback statement, no-sandbox-available, 403, proxy 5xx, and target 4xx rendered as data rather than as a portal error.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Every state here shares one non-negotiable property: the portal NEVER falls back to a production servers: entry. (a) sending: send disabled for the duration, no double-submit and no second quota unit. (b) [data-error='request-invalid']: the body is schema-checked locally, the request never leaves the browser and the quota meter does not move. (c) [data-http='429'][data-error='quota-exceeded']: the meter reads limit/limit with the danger fill, Retry-After and the reset time are shown, send stays DISABLED until reset with the reason on its accessible description, and catalog/spec reading is explicitly unaffected. (d) [data-error='sandbox-target-unavailable'] with data-http='503': carries [data-safety-note='no-prod-fallback'] stating the request was not sent anywhere else; the target selector shows [data-sandbox-health='down'] so the condition is visible BEFORE pressing send. (e) [data-error='sandbox-not-available']: no mock can be generated and the repo declared no x-fuzefront-sandbox-url — absence of opt-in means mock-only, never production; send is disabled and explained. (f) [data-http='403'][data-error='playground-forbidden']: Permit denied DevPortalPlayground:use while catalog reading keeps working. (g) [data-error='proxy-error']: 5xx from devportal-service itself, surfaces a copyable [data-request-id] and states no quota was consumed. (h) [data-state='target-error-response']: a 4xx/5xx FROM THE TARGET is a successful sandbox call and renders in the response panel as data — only the portal's own failures use StatusCallout. Conflating the two trains developers to ignore errors.

frames.label: 09 · My access (membership / quota / sandbox keys + states)
frames.summary: Root-org Developer membership with an explicit grants / does-not-grant split, sandbox quota with per-target breakdown, sandbox keys with reveal-once and revoke, plus provisioning, denied (403), empty, error and revoke-confirm states.
frames.acceptanceNotes: GET /me/access. [data-panel='membership'] states the organization (platform root), [data-membership-role='developer'], how and when it was granted, and the signing identity. [data-scope='developer'] renders BOTH halves: [data-scope-grants='allowed'] (DevPortalCatalog:read, DevPortalPlayground:use, DevPortalPlayground:view_history) and [data-scope-grants='denied'] (no tenant data, no administration, no other developer's history) — showing only what a role grants is how people assume it grants more. [data-panel='quota'] repeats the meter with a per-target breakdown. [data-panel='sandbox-keys'] lists masked keys with created/last-used and per-row [data-action='revoke-key']; creation surfaces [data-reveal='once'] whose copy states the value is shown exactly once and is stored hashed. Revoke is confirmed explicitly ([data-state='revoke-confirm']), never one-click. Three account states are contract: [data-membership-status='provisioning'] on a very first sign-in — catalog and playground stay disabled until the grant lands rather than appearing to work and then 403-ing; [data-membership-status='denied'] with data-http='403' when provisioning failed or the flag audience excludes the account, failing closed as a whole rather than exposing a subset; and [data-error='access-load-failed'], where nothing is rendered from a default or cached assumption.
